nodes.label: Birch Design Lab (Year-One Legal Name)
nodes.rationale: Won because the three-word form is the only candidate that is a complete sentence and follows the surname+trade+workplace naming formula (Johnson Printing Works, Wright Brothers Cycle Shop); earns its length by telling a non-technical business owner who/what/where in one breath; passed the phone-answer test.

nodes.label: Birch Labs (Established-Era Name)
nodes.rationale: Natural erosion once referrals do the explaining; carries the Bell Labs institutional echo and science sentiment.

nodes.label: Birch (Eventual Spoken Name)
nodes.rationale: The spoken name was never a choice — no one says the suffix out loud; what clients will have been calling it all along.

nodes.label: BDL (Initialism)
nodes.rationale: Quiet monogram use only.

nodes.label: Word-Association Triad (Who/What/Where)
nodes.rationale: Birch = who (the founder), Design = what (the good sold), Lab = where (the bench); the 'feels twenty years old' filter was pointing at this structure the whole time. Rhythm: BIRCH-de-SIGN-LAB, ending on two hard beats like a door closing.

nodes.label: Etymological Line (beorc → bright)
nodes.rationale: Old English beorc, from a root meaning 'to shine' (same syllable as 'bright'); birch is the shining tree, white against dark wood, first to return after fire, the threshold tree of the north.

nodes.label: The Founding Myth (Pioneer Species + Birch-Bark Paper)
nodes.rationale: Birch is a pioneer species that stabilizes ground after fire; birch bark is the oldest paper of the north (Novgorod medieval letters survived 800 years). For a business building surfaces where small companies speak to the world, that is the job description growing in the yard.
nodes.norm_label: the founding myth (pioneer species + birch-bark paper)

nodes.label: The Credo
nodes.rationale: "First green after the fire — and the bark you write on." — one-sentence distillation of the founding myth.

nodes.label: The Chiaroscuro Principle
nodes.rationale: The word forks tonally (shining renewal vs. the disciplinary birch rod/fasces). Verdict: the fork is the aesthetic — quiet luxury is chiaroscuro. Drives the light/dark-mode-native identity decision, with dark mode as the founder's default face.

nodes.label: The Surname Effect
nodes.rationale: "Birch built our site" parses as a person built it; surname-based firms read as established by default — a referral-economy advantage no other candidate had. Reinforced by the founder physically resembling the namesake tree (tall, pale, suited to the north).

nodes.label: The Fathom Sentence (Retained Meaning)
nodes.rationale: "To measure the unknown using yourself as the ruler." The line that started the entire search stays in the brand's private mythology though the Fathom name did not survive; usable in about-page/process copy without naming it.

nodes.label: Grand Seiko White Birch (SLGH005) — North Star Object
nodes.rationale: Bark texture rendered in metal; luxury that whispers, restraint everywhere — the visual register handed to the eventual designer.
nodes.norm_label: grand seiko white birch (slgh005) — north star object

nodes.label: Lenticel Dashes (Mark Concept)
nodes.rationale: The horizontal bark marks — instantly birch, fully abstract, doubles as lines of text/writing; only light-field identity in a market of dark-navy dev shops, ownable.

nodes.label: The Graveyard, Final Edition
nodes.rationale: Retired candidates with causes of death: Fathom (name already claimed by multiple firms), Helm (weak phonetic onset/coda, fails phone test), Harbor (hijacked ear — Harbor Freight, care-industry warmth), Sound (killed twice — Sound Lab reads as recording studio), Keel ('keel over' idiom dominates locally; KeelWorks claimed), Birchworks/fused forms (ch-w seam stumbles), double suffixes (Works/Lab/Studio/Design never stack), plus an earlier graveyard (Current, Tidal, Delta, Flux, Apex, Nautilus, Range, Arbor, Root, Cascade, Vantage, Strata).

nodes.label: The Epic Framework (Lesson of Record)
nodes.rationale: Built to find the sublime, it did its job by failing — overruled by three things it had no columns for: the mouth, the market, and the founder's actual affections; its real function was to exhaust every alternative until the honest answer was the only one standing.

nodes.label: The Mouth Lens (Decisive Lesson)
nodes.rationale: A service firm's name is a sound event in other people's mouths — referrals, phone static, local accents. Test phonetic onset/coda, semantic hijack, the referral sentence, and the phone answer; plosive onsets read solid, B is the sturdiest in the language.

nodes.label: Three Legs: Myth, Mouth, Availability
nodes.rationale: Every candidate needed all three legs. Birch was the only word that ended with all three present (myth thinnest but real, mouth strongest, field most scattered).

nodes.label: Outstanding Admin (Domains, Trademark, LLC, Visual Identity)
nodes.rationale: Remaining tasks: check birchdesignlab.com and fallback domains immediately; USPTO TESS knockout search under Class 42; LLC filing as Birch Design Lab; register social handles; visual identity work led by founder with a graphics person.
nodes.norm_label: outstanding admin (domains, trademark, llc, visual identity)

nodes.label: The Brief
nodes.rationale: Solo software + web development business for non-technical clients; what a name pings in a developer's head was explicitly ruled irrelevant. Goal: depth, meaning, symbolism, history — a brand epic, touchstone example Fathom = 'to measure the unknown using yourself as the ruler.'

nodes.label: The Naming System (Suffix Format)
nodes.rationale: [Word] Design Lab / Solution Lab(s) / Design(s) / Lab(s), eventually just [Word]; the suffix is a lever controlling the initialism and domain.

nodes.label: The Design Filter (Surface Test)
nodes.rationale: Short (1-3 syllables), feels established not 2024-startup, signals competence not creativity-for-its-own-sake, layered/multiple meaning. Rejects overly literal names and corny puns.

nodes.label: The Brand Epic (Decisive Lens)
nodes.rationale: Midway through, this overrode the surface filter: the brand's spine is the sublime — human competence set against overwhelming force. Test: is there a human in the picture, and are they in the struggle, above it, or sheltered from it?

nodes.label: Conflict Frames (Man vs. God/Nature/Self/Society)
nodes.rationale: Priority order: man vs god (favorite), man vs nature (favorite), man vs self (favorite, added later), man vs society (not a priority), cute/voice-driven branding explicitly not the approach.

nodes.label: The Graveyard (Cut Words)
nodes.rationale: Current, Tidal, Delta, Flux, Apex, Nautilus cut for distinctiveness collisions; Sound too common to own; Range generic; Arbor too soft; Root contested ownership; Cascade no protagonist/struggle and real-world firm collisions; Vantage reads cheesy/techy; Strata too abstract, no human actor.

nodes.label: Fathom — The Mind (Finalist)
nodes.rationale: OE fæðm, the span of outstretched arms, a body-measure to sound the sea's depth. Bedrock meaning: take the measure of the unknown using yourself as the ruler. Verb: to understand — most intellectual of the four. Most crowded name commercially (Fathom Software LLC, Fathom Analytics, etc.). Tagline: 'Depth you can build on.' Initialism FDL.

nodes.label: Helm — The Will (Finalist)
nodes.rationale: Root helma (tiller) + helmaz (helmet); Greek cousin kybernetes (steersman) -> govern, cybernetics. Verb: to command. Most complete name, works across all four frames including man vs society (ship of state). Tagline: 'Steady at the helm.' Initialism HDL.

nodes.label: Harbor — The Heart (Finalist)
nodes.rationale: OE herebeorg = army + shelter, a refuge built because the host is under threat. Verb: to keep. Casts a different protagonist — you are the place the storm is survived, the keeper, not the operator. Tagline: 'A safe harbor for your ideas.' Initialism HSL.

nodes.label: Birch — Stands Apart (Finalist)
nodes.rationale: Root beorc (birch-rune of renewal) from PIE bhereg- 'to shine, bright, white' — the shining tree. Epic is renewal, not struggle (pioneer species, first green after fire) — sits a step outside the favored confrontation frame. Literary anchor: Frost's Birches. Tonal instability: to birch = to flog, the fasces. Most personal word, least control over symbolism. Tagline: 'Fine-grained work.' Initialism BSL.

nodes.label: Four-Frame Re-Ranking
nodes.rationale: Fathom & Helm lead man-vs-god/nature; man-vs-self levels out across all four; man-vs-society nearly inverts (Strata/Helm/Harbor/Birch lead, Fathom trails). Helm is the only word that never leaves the table across all frames.

nodes.label: Practical Reality Checks (Collision, Domains, Trademark)
nodes.rationale: All four finalists already in use by web/design shops elsewhere; severity worst-to-least: Fathom, Helm, Harbor, Birch. No usable .lab/.labs TLD exists — suffix must go in the domain or use .studio/.design/.dev/etc. Trademark would file in Class 42; not cleared without USPTO TESS search.

nodes.label: Suggested Next Steps
nodes.rationale: Commission a construction pass on the live list (founding myth, credo, etymological line) plus initial visual/color translation; run USPTO Class 42 TESS search and lock the domain form before committing.
